title: Are protection plans worth it?
summary: A consumer news segment examines whether protection plans/extended warranties on electronics, appliances and cars are worth buying, citing a Consumer Reports survey.

assertions.quote: MANY TIMES PLANS ONLY PAY FOR HARDWARE ISSUES, NOT WHAT CAUSES MOST ISSUES LIKE VIRUSES

verdicts.note: Hardware-only coverage is standard for device protection plans, but the claim that 'most issues' are software-caused is a generalization that varies by device type and use

assertions.quote: YOUR DEVICE MAY NOT EVEN HAVE A RECORD BREAKING DOWN DURING THE WARRANTY PERIOD
THE MEDIAN COST OF REPAIRS JUST $3 MORE THAN THE COST OF THE PLAN

verdicts.note: This reflects the same Consumer Reports survey finding that median repair costs roughly matched the plan price, indicating little net financial benefit on average

Abito & Salant's structural estimate finds TV extended-warranty profit margins of 62%-73%, meaning the expected cost of repairs is only about 27%-38% of the warranty's price -- a clear minority, not "about the same as the price" as the claim states.

assertions.quote: APPLE HAS BASICALLY DONE EVERYTHING THEY CAN TO MAKE IT VIRTUALLY IMPOSSIB LEFOR ANYBODY OTHER THAN THEM TO FIX

verdicts.note: Apple's repair restrictions do raise independent-repair costs, making AppleCare comparatively more valuable, but this is an argued interpretation rather than an independently measured value comparison

assertions.quote: MAKE SURE IT COVERS SPILLS AND DROPS

verdicts.note: This is straightforward, verifiable due-diligence advice consistent with standard consumer-protection guidance
